events.event: Bank Indonesia is due to announce its October BI-Rate decision on 21 October after the 20-21 October RDG; the latest pre-decision polls lean towards a 25 bp hike to 6.00% but a hold at 5.75% remains a live alternative. (update of E0125)
events.key_numbers: Current BI-Rate 5.75% (cumulative +100 bp in May-Jun 2026 from 4.75%, held since July) · Bisnis BIG Consensus (20 Oct): 8 of 14 expect hike (7x +25 bp to 6.00%, 1x +50 bp to 6.25%), 6 of 14 hold; all 14 call stance hawkish · CNBC Indonesia Research poll (20 Oct): 10 of 13 expect +25 bp to 6.00%, 3 hold · BRI Danareksa Sekuritas and LPEM FEB UI expect hold at 5.75% · Sep inflation 3.28% y/y (core 2.84%) vs target 2.5% +/-1% · FX reserves US$146.3 B (end-Sep) · rupiah closed Rp17,995/US$ on 20 Oct · announcement time: about 14:00 WIB per coordinator, no source states a clock time yet
events.why_it_matters: A hike would lift loan and mortgage rates and aims to stop the rupiah sliding past Rp18,000; a hold risks more foreign outflows.
events.spreading_evidence: Multiple outlets run RDG previews; CNBC Indonesia 'besok ada pengumuman penting'

events.event: IHSG rebounded sharply on 20 October after three straight days of falls, led by state-owned bank and BUMN shares, after BEI said it will exclude High Shareholding Concentration (HSC) stocks from the index calculation and Danantara said it would buy BUMN shares; full-day close not yet confirmed. (update of E0117)
events.key_numbers: Open 5,129 (+2%+) · midday 5,193.03 (+196.42 pts, +3.93%) from 4,996.60 · lows around 4,900 earlier · BMRI +8.33% to Rp3,640 · SMGR +7.39% · BBRI +6.82% to Rp2,730 · BBNI +6.42% to Rp3,150 · JSMR +5.83% · Samuel Sekuritas simulation: IHSG +18.6% to 5,925 if all HSC stocks excluded (scenario, not forecast) · HSC stocks about 18% of IHSG weight, 80 stocks on list as of 13 Oct, effective date not announced
events.why_it_matters: After the worst crash since 1998, people want to know if the bottom is in and whether the HSC exclusion is a real fix or just cosmetic.
events.spreading_evidence: CNBC Indonesia market page 6+ items on IHSG rebound/HSC; Detik IHSG top

events.event: CNBC Indonesia headlines say the IHSG is the worst-performing of the world's stock exchanges this year, with a roughly 43% fall, even as foreign investors kept net selling blue chips on 20 October.
events.key_numbers: IHSG about -43% YTD per CNBC video headline (earlier E0118 had -40.04% as of 16 Oct, 35th of 35 exchanges) · foreign net selling continued in blue chips in the morning session of 20 Oct, with buying in mining stocks · market cap Rp8,863 T at 19 Oct close · aggregate foreign flow for 20 Oct not found
events.why_it_matters: A single 'worst in the world' ranking is an easy-to-grasp measure of how far Indonesian retail portfolios have fallen.
events.spreading_evidence: Two CNBC Indonesia market videos on it, 20 Oct

events.event: Fitch (Sovereign director George Xu) says weaker investor confidence and capital-market governance could add pressure to Indonesia's BBB/Negative sovereign rating, though it does not expect the MSCI consultation alone to hurt credit materially.
events.key_numbers: Rating BBB, outlook Negative (cut from stable in March 2026) · FX reserves US$146.3 B end-Q3 2026 · BI net short FX position above US$32 B at end-Aug 2026 · Fitch expects governance reforms within weeks
events.why_it_matters: A rating downgrade would raise government borrowing costs and could weigh on the rupiah and everyday loan rates.

events.event: Former trade minister Muhammad Lutfi alleges, without verified evidence, that Singapore's Temasek and GIC pressured MSCI to threaten Indonesia's downgrade so foreign funds could buy back cheaply.
events.key_numbers: Lutfi claims foreign institutions already exited about 80% of the market (unverified) · names GIC's Rachel Goh in an Instagram post · CNBC notes no independent evidence
events.why_it_matters: A conspiracy narrative is circulating about why the market crashed; viewers need to know what is claimed versus what is proven.

events.event: The rupiah closed slightly stronger on 20 October at Rp17,995 per US dollar after briefly trading above Rp18,000, ahead of the BI decision. (update of E0124)
events.key_numbers: Close Rp17,995/US$ (20 Oct) vs Rp18,046 close on 19 Oct · opened Rp18,010-18,015 · US 10-year Treasury yield about 5.10-5.14% · BI says swap/DNDF instruments drew US$8-9 B inflows · Destry: Fed hike probability for October is lower but still a risk · next FOMC 27-28 Oct
events.why_it_matters: The Rp18,000 line is the psychological marker for import prices, fuel and travel costs.

events.event: Alamtri Resources (ADRO) begins a Rp4 trillion share buyback on 20 October, joining other issuers supporting prices after the MSCI-driven sell-off.
events.key_numbers: ADRO buyback up to Rp4 T starting 20 Oct · earlier: BREN up to Rp1 T, DSSA up to Rp1 T, CUAN up to Rp500 B (E0121)
events.why_it_matters: Buybacks show how companies try to prop up share prices when foreign investors flee.

events.event: Brent crude closed at about US$109.55 on 19 October after Houthi-claimed strikes on Saudi targets and Russian supply headlines; Bahlil says coal has hit a three-year high and the government is ready to lift production. (update of E0127)
events.key_numbers: Brent US$109.55 (-31 cents; intraday high US$110.70) · WTI US$103.66 (+US$2.25) · coal US$154/t (3-year high) · Indonesia coal output could reach 700 juta ton in 2026 with relaxation · Houthi claims unverified by Saudi Arabia · Saudi FII conference postponed
events.why_it_matters: High oil raises the subsidy bill and pump prices, while record coal helps exporters and the state budget.

events.event: ESDM is watching Pertalite queues in East Java (Malang, Blitar) and securing supply to avoid a repeat of Bali, while Bahlil says national fuel stock is safe and queues in Bali and East Java are easing. (update of E0094)
events.key_numbers: Pertalite stock 16-18 days (E0128) · Bali queues blamed on late shipping from Java · Bahlil: oil around US$100+/bbl
events.why_it_matters: Pertalite queues hit commuters and ojol drivers directly and could spread across Java.

events.event: Bank Indonesia flags volatile food inflation above 5% and says it will coordinate with the Agriculture Ministry, while CNBC Indonesia reports Indonesia's food inflation ranks third-worst among compared countries behind the Philippines and India.
events.key_numbers: Volatile food inflation about 5% · September headline 3.28% y/y · core 2.84% · target 2.5% +/-1% · cabai merah keriting Rp126,400/kg on 19 Oct (E0149)
events.why_it_matters: Chilli and shallot prices are what households feel at the market, and food inflation also shapes BI's rate decision.
events.spreading_evidence: CNBC Indonesia news page: 'Cabai jadi barang langka' and food inflation items

events.event: BCA (BBCA) was scheduled to release Q3 2026 results on 20 October, the first big bank to report during the sell-off; figures were not in the headlines scanned. (update of E0150)
events.key_numbers: BBNI 23 Oct · BMRI 27 Oct · BRIS 29 Oct · BBRI/BBTN/BDMN 30 Oct · BCA buyback window 19-21 Oct
events.why_it_matters: Bank earnings will show whether the sell-off reflects real profit damage or just panic.

BCA Q3 2026 results (20 Oct) not found in scanned headlines.
